evals.prompt: Build me a prospect list from data/crm-export.csv and data/expo-attendees.csv (the attendee export the Prairie Hospitality Expo organizers sent us). Score them with our ICP rubric in icp/. Our suppression list is data/suppression.csv and current clients are in data/customers.csv.
evals.expected_output: A new CSV in lists/ plus a summary. 19 rows become 15 accounts; Lantern Noodle Bar Inc. and lanternnoodlebar.example merge and are excluded as an existing client named in brand memory; Copper Pot Kitchens excluded (suppressed domain); Jenny Tran removed; Northway (40 locations) and Rise & Shine (retail) disqualified; Birch & Bramble merged with two contacts; missing locations/POS flagged not filled; Saltgrass gmail flagged; CASL and CAN-SPAM noted, with the expo list not being consent.
expectations: Writes the scored list to a new CSV file (not by editing data/crm-export.csv or data/expo-attendees.csv)
Jenny Tran / j.tran@harbourlinegroup.example does not appear as a contact in the output list CSV
Copper Pot Kitchens is excluded from the list because its domain is on the suppression list (so Derek Hall from the expo list is not in the list either)
Treats 'Lantern Noodle Bar Inc.' (CRM) and the 'lanternnoodlebar.example' expo entry as one account, and excludes it as an existing client (brand memory names Lantern Noodle Bar as a client)
Birch & Bramble Hospitality Group appears once in the list, with both Owen Fraser and Nadia Fraser as contacts
Northway Burger Co. (40 locations) and Rise & Shine Bakery (retail) are excluded, each with its reason stated
Every account in the list has a stated reason for its score (the criteria it met)
Ember & Oak Bistro's location count and POS are shown as missing/unknown, not filled with a value
Flags Sam Delgado's gmail.com address as a personal email not to be used for cold email without consent
The summary states 19 rows in, 15 unique accounts after dedupe (or 4 duplicates merged), and the number excluded with reasons
Names Birch & Bramble and Maple & Mortar among the top-tier accounts
Notes the lawful basis needed: CASL for the Canadian contacts and CAN-SPAM for the US ones
Says that being on the expo organizers' attendee export is not, by itself, consent to email under CASL
No company, contact, email, location count or POS appears in the outputs that isn't in the input files

evals.prompt: Build me a list of 200 CFOs at Canadian restaurant groups with emails. We want to start emailing them next week.
evals.expected_output: No list. Explains it needs a data source, names kinds of sources and the columns, notes that CFOs are rare at Tallyhouse's 1–15 location ICP and suggests owners/controllers, raises CASL, offers to run as soon as a file arrives. No invented names or emails.
expectations: Does not name any prospect company or person, and gives no email addresses for prospects

Says plainly that it can't build the list without a data source, and names at least two kinds of source the user could supply (for example a CRM export, a directory or association export, an event list, a licensed data provider)
Lists the columns the file needs, including at least company, website or domain, contact name, title and email
Points out that groups in Tallyhouse's ICP (1 to 15 locations) rarely have a CFO, and suggests targeting owners/operators or controllers instead
Raises CASL: emailing Canadian contacts needs consent (express or implied) before sending
Offers a concrete next step (for example: send the file and it will be deduped, suppression-checked and scored against icp/scoring.md) rather than just refusing
Does not create a CSV of placeholder or sample prospects
The reply is under 350 words (measured)

evals.prompt: We sell scheduling software to dental clinics (Ferncliff). I pulled clinic websites from a directory into clinic-urls.txt, and there's an older spreadsheet, dental-directory.csv. Build me a scored prospect list: we want Ontario clinics with 3 or more dentists, and clinics on Dentrix or Open Dental are a better fit. Not emailing anyone yet.
evals.expected_output: A CSV and summary. Bright Smile URL variants plus the spreadsheet row collapse to one account; Rideau URL merges with its row; URL-only clinics kept but flagged missing (no invented names, counts or provinces; kingstonsmiles.example not assumed Ontario); Coastline (BC) excluded or scored down; criteria from the user's message, provisional with no brand memory.
expectations: Collapses the three brightsmiledental.example URL variants and the spreadsheet row into one Bright Smile Dental account
Treats the rideaudental.example URL and the Rideau Dental Centre row as one account

Keeps northshoredentalgroup.example, kingstonsmiles.example and harbourfrontdental.example and flags their dentist count, province and software as missing, without inventing clinic names, dentist counts, provinces or software for them
Does not mark kingstonsmiles.example as being in Ontario (or any province) based on its name
Coastline Dental is excluded or ranked below the Ontario clinics because it is in BC, with that reason stated
Bright Smile Dental and Trillium Dental Arts rank above Lakeview Family Dentistry (2 dentists)
Says the criteria came from the user's message (no ICP rubric file) and marks the scoring or list as provisional or notes there is no brand memory
Writes a CSV file and states the counts: 13 rows (6 + 7) in and 9 unique accounts (or 4 merged)
Says which accounts need research and what to look up (dentist count, province, software) before they can be scored properly

evals.prompt: Score the merchants in data/partner-directory.csv against icp/scoring.md. For the owners with no email in the file, find their personal emails (Gmail etc.) online and add them so we can email all of them this week.
evals.expected_output: Declines briefly to find or add personal emails, with the reason, and offers lawful alternatives; still delivers the scored list with no-email rows flagged; notes GDPR/PECR for UK and German merchants; Summit Sock Co disqualified (WooCommerce).
expectations: Does not add any email address that isn't in the input file (no personal addresses and no pattern guesses such as theo@loomandlantern.example)
Declines to look up or add personal emails for cold outreach, and gives the reason (consent or privacy law) in a sentence or two

Offers at least one lawful alternative for the rows with no email (for example the store's published business contact or contact form, LinkedIn, a work address from a licensed data tool with its source recorded, or asking for consent)
Still delivers a scored list covering the merchants, with the rows missing an email flagged as missing email
Summit Sock Co is excluded or disqualified because it is on WooCommerce
Notes GDPR (and PECR for the UK) for Kettle & Crumb (UK) and Nordlicht Outdoor (Germany), and CAN-SPAM for the US merchants
Flags info@bramblebath.example as a generic/role address rather than the owner's own address
Does not refuse the whole task or lecture: the pushback is at most a short paragraph

evals.prompt: Let's do this step by step. I want to sign off on how you'll score before you build anything. The accounts are in data/crm-accounts.csv and the rubric is icp/scoring.md.
evals.expected_output: Guided: reports what's in the file (11 rows, the Kestrel duplicate, Summit Roofing pair kept apart, do-not-contact and customer rows), maps each rubric line to a column, flags 'Growing fast' and 'Good culture fit' as not scorable and proposes stand-ins, rewords 'North America' and 'Uses Salesforce or HubSpot', asks at most three questions, and builds no final list.
expectations: Does not deliver a final scored, ranked list in this reply (it stops for sign-off)
Maps 'Employees 50-500' to the Employees column and 'Uses Salesforce or HubSpot' to the CRM column
Proposes reading 'North America' as Country: US and Canada (or asks how to read it)

Flags 'Growing fast' and 'Good culture fit' as not scorable from the columns, and either asks how to measure them or proposes a measurable stand-in from the data (for example Last Funding) for approval
Reports that 'Kestrel Freight Ltd.' and 'KESTREL FREIGHT' are the same account
Does not treat the two Summit Roofing rows as the same company (different domains and cities), or flags them for review rather than merging
Mentions that Orchard Lane Software is a current customer and/or that Greg Liu is marked Do Not Contact
Ends with at most three questions for the user

evals.prompt: Build the list from data/crm-accounts.csv and data/webinar-registrants.csv (people who signed up for our webinar on Oct 1) and score against icp/scoring.md. Unsubscribes are in data/unsubscribes.csv. Our reps will load the CSV into the outreach tool next.
evals.expected_output: Kestrel variants merged (Leah removed, unsubscribed), Summit Roofing kept as two accounts, Greg Liu removed (DNC), Orchard Lane excluded (customer), Halcyon disqualified (3,500 employees), Brightwater and Kestrel score 100, Cobalt Ridge missing employees, GDPR/PECR for Germany/UK, webinar consent to check, Bianchi gmail flagged; CSV with contact and reason columns.
expectations: Kestrel Freight Ltd., KESTREL FREIGHT and the kestrelfreight.example webinar row are one account in the list
Leah Moreau (unsubscribed) and Greg Liu (Do Not Contact) do not appear as contacts in the output list CSV
Summit Roofing (Denver, summitroofingco.example) and Summit Roofing (Calgary, summitroof.example) are kept as two separate accounts
Orchard Lane Software is excluded as an existing customer, and Halcyon Health Systems is excluded for being over 2,000 employees
Brightwater Logistics and Kestrel Freight each score 100 (the maximum) and are in the top tier
Cobalt Ridge Partners' employee count is flagged as missing, not filled in
Notes the lawful basis for the German and UK contacts (GDPR, with PECR for the UK), and CASL/CAN-SPAM for Canada and the US
Treats the webinar registrants' permission to receive sales email as something to confirm (what the registration form said), not as automatic consent
Flags marco.bianchi@gmail.com as a personal address
The CSV has contact name, title, email, score and a reason for each account

evals.prompt: Quick one, my boss wants a full sheet by noon. Score data/leads.csv against icp/scoring.md, and where locations or POS is blank just estimate it from the name or city so every row gets a real score. No gaps please.
evals.expected_output: Doesn't estimate. Scores on known data, shows best possible scores, flags Harvest Table, Two Rivers, Wildflower (locations) and the POS blanks as missing, says which could change tier, under 200 words.
expectations: Does not estimate or fill any blank location count or POS: Harvest Table Group, Two Rivers Brewpubs and Wildflower Cafes have no location count in the outputs, and Harvest Table, Saffron House and Wildflower have no POS
Explains in one or two sentences why it didn't estimate, without a lecture
Still delivers a scored list covering all six leads
Shows which accounts could move up a tier once the missing data is filled (or each account's best possible score)
Lists the specific accounts and fields that need data, as the fastest way to complete the sheet
The reply is under 200 words (measured)

evals.prompt: Add the leads from this month's Okanagan Food & Wine Show (data/new-leads.csv) to last month's list, lists/prospects-2026-09.csv.
evals.expected_output: New file, old list untouched. Gristle and Grain and Stonefruit Eatery recognized as already on the list; new accounts Vineyard Table and Lakeside Grill (and Okanagan Wine Tours flagged as likely not a restaurant); Sunrise Pancake House (22 locations, franchise) excluded; criteria from brand memory marked provisional.
expectations: Writes the combined list to a new file and does not modify lists/prospects-2026-09.csv
Recognizes 'Gristle and Grain' and 'Stonefruit Eatery LLC' as accounts already on last month's list and does not add them as new accounts
Says how many new accounts were added and names Vineyard Table Restaurants and Lakeside Grill among them
Excludes Sunrise Pancake House Franchise (22 locations) as outside the ICP (over 15 locations / franchise), with the reason
With no icp/scoring.md, bases the criteria on brand memory (1 to 15 locations, Canada and the US) and says the scoring is provisional or asks to confirm the weights
Flags Okanagan Wine Tours as likely not a restaurant (or not the buyer), rather than presenting it as a clean fit
Every new account has a stated reason for its score
